title: The Doctrine of Justification: Westminster Confession Chapter 11
speaker: Elder Scott Hollander

outline.title: Defining Key Terms: Justice, Mercy, and Grace
subpoints: Justice is receiving what one deserves (wrath for sin).
Mercy is not receiving the deserved punishment.
Grace is receiving an undeserved gift (Christ's righteousness).

outline.title: The Timing of Justification: Decree vs. Execution
subpoints: Justification is not from eternity past, though decreed then.
Distinction between God's plan and its historical application.
Believers are condemned until they believe (John 3:18).

outline.title: Justification is Applied by Faith, Not Merely at the Cross
subpoints: Christ's work secured justification, but it is applied in time.
Context of Romans 4 shows imputation occurs upon belief.
Faith is the instrument that receives Christ's righteousness.

summary:
In this session of the Westminster Standards series, Elder Scott Hollander examines Chapter 11 of the Confession of Faith, focusing on the doctrine of justification. The teaching begins by clarifying the theological distinctions between justice, mercy, and grace, emphasizing that justification is an act of free grace where Christ's righteousness is imputed to the believer. The primary focus is on the timing of justification, specifically addressing and correcting the error that the elect are justified from eternity past. While God's decree to justify the elect is eternal, the execution of that decree occurs in time through the work of the Holy Spirit and the believer's faith.

The sermon refutes the notion that justification is complete at the moment of the cross or the resurrection alone, arguing instead that it is applied to the individual when they place their faith in Christ. Using passages such as John 3:18 and Romans 4, the teaching highlights that believers remain under condemnation until they believe, and that the imputation of righteousness is contingent upon faith. This distinction preserves the sovereignty of God's eternal plan while affirming the necessity of personal faith and repentance for the application of salvation.
